newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 24.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
LEFT FEARS SNAP POLL

The stability of the government has become uncertain with the Congress party and the Left becoming wary of each other's future moves. Senior Left leaders were believed to have warned their United Front (UF) colleagues that they should begin preparations for elections possibly within a year. The Left feared the Congress may not allow the UF to stabilise. A section of the Congress was also putting pressure on the party leadership not to enter into any coordination arrangements.
The Economic Times
CORE SECTOR OUTPUT FAILS TO HIT THE TARGET

Fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) showed serious shortages in core sector inputs. The latest statistics reveal the core sector further deteriorated during the December 1996-February 1997 period. Indigenous crude production fell during the period by three percent from the April-December 1996 figures. Power generation fell short by 1.4 percent, coal by 2.1 percent, fertilisers by five percent, saleable steel by five percent and cement by 0.8 percent.
MUTUAL FUNDS FIND NOTHING TO BANK ON IN APEX BANK'S POLICY

Mutual funds which launched assured return funds were in a fix due to a reduction in interest rates after the announcement of the credit policy, and a consequent lowering of rates by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The schemes were conceived at the time when rates were higher than current levels. But the recent rate cuts would force them to deploy their funds in various instruments only at rates lower than anticipated.
BUDGET HAS FAILED TO TEAR DOWN BARRIERS: U.S. TRADE OFFICE

The United States is critical of India's trade policies and tariff structure despite a 'dream budget' for 1997/98 (April-March). The National Trade Estimate of India (1997) noted that despite recent tariff reductious and relaxation of quantitative curbs, restrictions on consumer goods imports, quantitative restrictions under the restricted imports list and high tariffs remained serious impediments to U.S. trade, especially in agricultural and consumer items.
U.S. PARTNER MAY GET MAJORITY IN LUBRIZOL

The Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) is likely to sell a majority of the stake in Lubrizol India that it is buying from the government, to Lubrizol Corporation of the United States. The procedure was in line with the recommendations of the Disinvestment Commission which favoured the government disinvesting in favour of a strategic partner, which was then at liberty to sell the stake. The arrangement was likely to see Lubrizol Corp attaining a majority holding in Lubrizol India.
Financial Express
FINANCE MINISTRY BLOCKS COGENTRIX COUNTER-GUARANTEE

The Finance Ministry has refused to formalise the counter-guarantee cover given to the 1,000 megawatt Cogentrix power project in Karnataka. This would effectively stall the project as the promoters had refused to go ahead unless such a cover was made available. The ministry said the 59.58 million rupee power project was unviable. The complex, coming up in Mangalore, lacked a transmission network to evacuate power.
JAMES CAPEL FORECASTS UPTREND IN INFLATION

James Capel predicted a rise in inflation to nine percent, about 200 basis points higher, due to increased money supply and a rise in oil prices in the second half of 1997/98 (April-March). The investment banker also forecast an increase in industrial growth and upward pressure on prime lending rates of banks and a six percent depreciation of the rupee against the dollar. James Capel said money supply would grow at 17 percent in 1998 as compared to 15.6 percent in 1997.
Business Standard
STEEL AUTHORITY NET PROJECTED TO PLUNGE 50 PCT

Steel Authority of India's (SAIL) net profit for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) was estimated to fall to 6.53 billion rupees from 13.19 billion in 1995/96. The fall in profit would be due to a massive increase in input costs and interest payments. According to the performance budget of the Steel Ministry, the sharp fall was despite an estimated marginal increase in income from 157.3 billion rupees to 161 billion rupees during 1996/97.
COLGATE PALMOLIVE TO SET UP 100 PCT SUBSIDIARY IN NEPAL

Colgate-Palmolive (India) shareholders have approved the setting up of a 100-percent owned subsidiary in Nepal at an estimated cost of 280 million rupees. The shareholders also approved the expansion of the company's board to include two new directors and confirmation of N. Jayaraman as its new managing director in place of Jim Trigwell. Company sources said the subsidiary would make personal care, toilet and household products, mostly for the domestic market.
RBI GETS 50 BLN RUPEE PRIVATE PLACEMENT OF 10-YEAR PAPER

The government has announced a private placement of 50 billion rupees worth of 10-year paper at a coupon of 13.05 percent with the RBI. This was seen as an attempt by the RBI to correct the yield on the 10-year paper. The government would also float the first of the state government loans worth 25 billion rupees for fiscal 1997/98.
CABINET GROUP SEEKS REVIEW OF CURBS ON CROSS-MEDIA HOLDING

The ministerial group examining a cabinet note on the proposed broadcasting bill has recommended a review of the manner in which restrictions on cross-media holdings were proposed in the bill. The group suggested that the norms for satellite services, including direct-to-home networks, should be elaborated upon to ensure companies were prevented from operating without licences. The group suggested that uplinking from India be made mandatory for all types of services.
The Observer
HUTCHISON MAX SHELVES $125 MLN ADR ISSUE

Hutchison Max, the cellular telephone licence holder for Bombay, has decided to shelve its proposed $125 million ADR issue. Several factors, including underpricing of the issue by global investors, were understood to have forced the company to wrap up the issue. Hutchison Max was now weighing other options such as a term loan, private placement and equity participation for alternate funding.
PETROCHEM INDUSTRY HEADING FOR NEGATIVE GROWTH: STUDY

The petrochemical industry in India is heading for a negative growth in the coming years, according to James Capel. The downward phase is likely to begin from mid-1997 with a sharp drop in profit margins of petrochemical companies by eight percent in 1997/98 (April-March). Both the medium- and short-term outlook are dismal. However, the petrochemical industry has made rapid strides in the last four years in terms of growth in production and consumption ranging between 12 to 15 percent.
Business Line
GE CAPITAL OFFERS TOTAL BUY-OUT OF SRF FINANCE

GE Capital has made the first offer by a firm under the new takeover regulations to acquire an equity stake in SRF Finance. GE's revised offer to acquire the entire block of shares of SRF Finance was cleared by the capital market regulator, SEBI. Earlier, the company had offered to acquire 20 percent of the equity of SRF Finance after buying out the entire equity holding of 53 percent held by the promoters. The earlier offer by GE Capital was made in January when the new takeover code had not been notified.
